clue.text: Joe's excited touring sumptuous old city

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the jumbled name travels around the other piece
excited letters are stirred up, so the name Joe is jumbled

parts.note: the name Joe; the 's stands for 'is', linking it to 'excited'
sumptuous means rich

explanation.surface: Joe is thrilled to be travelling round a lavish ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joe's excited' reads as Joe is excited, so only the name is jumbled (JEO), and 'touring' sends it around the rich part; the 's is not part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Jericho is among the oldest continuously inhabited cities, in the West Bank.

clue.text: Record single does rock event

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
single means one, the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: to rock is to shake, so the letters of does are shaken up

explanation.surface: A record by a solo artist plays rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' rearranges DOES as SODE.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is an incident or happening, one event in a series.

clue.text: Objects to special police force turning up after lunchtime

indicators.note: after puts the reversed pieces behind the time

parts.note: lunchtime is one o'clock, 1 written as the Roman I

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means read from the bottom, so the pieces are reversed

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: Someone protests at a special police unit showing up after lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objects' looks like a verb (protests) but is the noun. 'turning up' reverses S and MET to TEMS, which comes 'after' I.
explanation.definitionFit: Items are individual articles or things, so the plural matches objects.

clue.text: More compassionate charioteer takes fake name

indicators.note: takes means takes in, so the charioteer holds the other piece

parts.note: Ben-Hur, the chariot-racing hero of the novel and film, shortened to Hur

indicators.note: fake means false, so the letters of name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kinder chariot driver adopts an assumed name.
explanation.walkthrough: The charioteer is Ben-Hur, trimmed to his surname; 'fake' jumbles NAME into a horse's MANE, which he 'takes' in. Humaner is a rare but valid comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: Humane means kind and merciful, so the comparative means kinder.

clue.text: Inspire soldiers to swim outside

indicators.note: outside tells us the swimming word sits round the soldiers

parts.note: to swim is to bathe
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Encourage the troops to go for a swim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspire' is used in its literal sense of drawing breath in, not its everyday sense of motivating someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire, literally, is to draw air into the lungs, which is what breathing in does.

clue.text: Sorry criminal steals archbishop's first beads

indicators.note: steals means takes in, so the jumbled letters hold the other piece
criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters of sorry are twisted
first means the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An apologetic thief takes the archbishop's prayer beads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges SORRY as ROSRY, which 'steals' the A from archbishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosary is a string of beads used to count prayers.

clue.text: Song about life and extremely dangerous places to land

parts.note: an air is a song or tune

indicators.note: about suggests moving around, so the letters of life are rearranged
extremely means at the extremes, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A song about life and very dangerous landing spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges LIFE as FIEL; 'extremely dangerous' gives DS.
explanation.definitionFit: Airfields are areas where aircraft take off and come down.

clue.text: Very small thing used to promote Reagan?

parts.note: hype is publicity used to promote something
Ron is short for Ronald, as in US president Ronald Reagan

explanation.surface: Something tiny is used to boost Reagan's image.
explanation.walkthrough: A hyperon is a heavy subatomic particle, so 'Very small' is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Subatomic particles such as this are about as tiny as physical things get.

clue.text: Inability to see small present at first: a bipolar issue?

indicators.note: at first means these pieces come at the front

parts.note: present means now, the current time
blindness is the inability to see

explanation.surface: A diagnosis that a sight problem relates to bipolar disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bipolar' means at the two poles, not the mood disorder: snow glare there damages the eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Glare from snow and ice at the North and South Poles causes temporary loss of sight, a problem polar explorers face.

clue.text: Document exchanges hands — it's too hot to handle

indicators.note: the left hand L is swapped for the right hand R, the two hands exchanging places

parts.note: a file is a document or dossier

explanation.surface: A sensitive paper is passed between people because nobody wants to hold it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanges hands' looks like a document being passed on; here L (left) becomes R (right). Fire is also a theme entry, from the Prodigy song Firestarter.
explanation.definitionFit: Flames are literally too hot to pick up, a playful descriptive definition.

clue.text: Football team's caught by trip arranged in writing

parts.note: Man U is short for Manchester United, an English football club; with the 's it gives MANUS
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the letters of trip are rearranged

explanation.surface: A football team arranges a trip, with the plans set down on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns TRIP into RIPT.
explanation.definitionFit: A manuscript is a piece of writing, especially an author's handwritten or typed text.

clue.text: It makes me sick when one's taken in by spoon-bending

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside the other piece
bending suggests the word spoon being twisted out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone is nauseated at being fooled by a spoon-bending stage act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bending' rearranges SPOON as POSON, and 'taken in by' puts I inside it. Poison is a Prodigy song, one of the puzzle's theme entries.
explanation.definitionFit: A toxic substance is something that makes a person ill when swallowed.

clue.text: Woman arrived before 10 with 19 or so fighters

indicators.note: before places the woman and arrival letters ahead of the number's letters
with simply adds the last piece on

parts.note: ARR is the abbreviation for arrived, as seen on timetables
the number 10 written as the digits one and nought, read as the letters I and O

indicators.note: 19 across's solution means stripped of clothes, so the words or so lose their outer letters

explanation.surface: A woman turns up ahead of number ten with nineteen or so combatants.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' is read as the shapes I and O. '19' points to 19 across, meaning stripped: 'or so' with its outer letters stripped leaves RS. Warriors is also a Prodigy track title, in the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Warriors are soldiers or combatants, people who fight in battle.

clue.text: Make a mistake to be wearing outrageous flares with transfers

indicators.note: to be wearing means to be inside, the way a body is inside clothes
outrageous suggests wildness, so the letters of flares are scrambled

parts.note: to make a mistake is to err

explanation.surface: It's a blunder to wear loud flared trousers along with transfer designs.
explanation.walkthrough: Flares are wide-bottomed trousers, so 'to be wearing' fits the surface; 'outrageous' jumbles them as REFALS around the mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A referral passes a patient or case on to someone else, a kind of transfer.

clue.text: Magician's striking entrance holding top hat

indicators.note: holding means having the next piece inside
striking suggests a dramatic rearrangement, so the letters of entrance are reshuffled
top means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A conjuror's dramatic entrance with a top hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' rearranges ENTRANCE as ENCANTER, 'holding' the H from 'top hat'; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchanter is a sorcerer or wizard who casts spells.

clue.text: Nothing is returned wrapped in paper and stone

indicators.note: wrapped in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

indicators.note: is returned means sent back, so the word for nothing is read backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing, a zero score

explanation.surface: An empty parcel comes back wrapped in paper with a stone inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is returned' reverses the zero score to LIN; 'wrapped in' puts that inside the pink-paged business paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Flint is a hard grey stone once struck to make sparks.

clue.text: Maybe cancan can be racy, wearing delightfully exotic tops

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the initials enclose the jumbled letters
tops are the first letters of the words
to be racy is to be lively and risqué, so the letters of can are made to kick about

explanation.surface: A cancan can be risqué when danced in exotic costumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cancan' is the definition by example, so the separate 'can' is the fodder; 'be racy' jumbles it (ANC) and 'wearing' puts it in the 'tops' of 'delightfully exotic'.
explanation.definitionFit: The cancan is an example of a dance, with its high kicks, hence 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Unscrupulous person's problem at Christie's?

definitions.meaning: Christie's is a London auction house, where goods are sold in lots, so a faulty item is a poor lot

explanation.walkthrough: Christie's is a London auction house that sells goods in lots.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel is called a rotten egg, a phrase meaning a dishonest rogue.

clue.text: Naked Chef — is he?

definitions.meaning: a chef stripped of his outer letters leaves he, so the chef is literally unclothed; also a nod to The Naked Chef, a TV cookery show

explanation.surface: Is the TV cook called The Naked Chef really unclothed?
explanation.walkthrough: The Naked Chef was Jamie Oliver's British TV cookery show. Take the outside letters off CHEF and HE is what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without clothes on is the plain meaning of naked.

clue.text: One who edits text about 6's queen

parts.note: re means about or concerning
6 is VI in Roman numerals, and the 's adds S
ER is Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: An editor working on a text about the sixth queen.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' looks like a cross-reference to 6 down but is just the number, VI.
explanation.definitionFit: A reviser goes over written material and amends it, the work of an editor.

clue.text: European uprising? At home, government's running away

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising reads bottom to top, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a Pole is a European, someone from Poland
in means at home
G is an abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: A revolt in Europe; at home, the government flees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' looks like a revolt; here it turns POLE upwards to ELOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloping is running off secretly to marry, so running away fits.

clue.text: Masses of work occupied footballer

indicators.note: occupied means filled, so the footballer's name has the work inside

parts.note: Pelé, the Brazilian football great
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Plenty of work kept the footballer busy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Masses' looks like a quantity; it is the noun meaning the populace.
explanation.definitionFit: The masses are ordinary people collectively, the general public.

clue.text: Gardner is hugged by admirer in plant

indicators.note: hugged by means held inside the arms of the other piece

parts.note: a fan is an admirer
Ava Gardner was a Hollywood film star
is is a form of the verb be

explanation.surface: A film star is embraced by an admirer at a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory but means a growing thing; 'hugged by' puts the film star and 'is' (as BE) inside the admirer.
explanation.definitionFit: The broad bean plant, also called the fava bean, is a legume grown for its seeds.

parts.note: split as 5, 00, 500, 00: Roman V for five, two noughts as OO, Roman D for five hundred, and two more noughts

explanation.walkthrough: The digits split into 5, 00, 500 and 00, read as Roman V, two Os, Roman D and two more Os. Voodoo People is a Prodigy song.
explanation.definitionFit: Voodoo is a religion associated with sorcery and spells, so it can stand for magic.

clue.text: Drunk worked hard — time to quit?

indicators.note: to quit means to leave, so the time letter is removed

parts.note: toiled means worked hard

explanation.surface: A tipsy worker decides it is time to quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to quit' removes T from TOILED.
explanation.definitionFit: Oiled is slang for tipsy or intoxicated, as if lubricated with drink.

clue.text: Mammals stay supple after exercising

indicators.note: exercising suggests moving about, so the letters of stay supple are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Keep flexible after a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercising' is the anagram signal; 'after' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The duck-billed platypus is an egg-laying mammal of Australia.

clue.text: Positioned face to the west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left, so the word is turned backwards

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock or watch

explanation.surface: Placed so that it faces west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the west' turns DIAL around.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid means put down or placed, as in laid the table.

clue.text: Course includes minimalist art, erroneously

indicators.note: includes signals that the answer is held within the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A study course takes in minimalist art, wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'minimaliST ART ERroneously'. 'Course' means a meal course, not a study course; Firestarter is a Prodigy song, completed with 10 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A starter is the first course of a meal, served before the main dish.

clue.text: Wonder how expert's homework attains low grade?

parts.note: a pro is an expert; the 's is possessive, belonging to homework

indicators.note: attains here means gets hold of, so the home-improvement letters take in the grade

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is work done on one's home
G was a low GCSE grade in British school exams

explanation.surface: How does an expert's homework manage only a poor mark?
explanation.walkthrough: 'homework' is read as home work, DIY. 'attains' puts G inside it. The Prodigy is the band behind the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A prodigy is a wonder, especially a child of extraordinary talent.
